title: Seerah — The Prophet’s Life
description: Little Muslim → Pro. Short questions connect episodes from the Prophet’s life with thoughtful teaching, communication, care across religious differences, human dignity, playful family companionship, children’s turns, respectful correction, brotherhood in Madinah, peacemaking, repayment, market honesty, hospitality, wise advice, simple transport, encouragement of Ibn Abbas, practical prayer guidance, the people of Suffah, modest living, lasting friendship and balanced responsibilities. An adult may read questions aloud or explain unfamiliar names and words. All questions are Pro level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Pro is the highest editorial level within Little Muslim, not the Educated User level. It asks children to connect a narrated event with its purpose, distinguish a supported conclusion from an overstatement, and apply a lesson to a short situation. The three styles are question formats, not difficulty tiers. No specialist historical disputes, obscure dates, legal details or memorization of hadith reference numbers is required. The bank has not been calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: The cited reports from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim and the footrace report in Sunan Abi Dawud were checked during preparation. The linked Abi Dawud 2578 page labels that report Sahih according to Al-Albani; this is a source attribution, not independent authentication. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Present-day scenarios are illustrative applications and are not claimed as narrated events. The visit to the sick Jewish boy is used to teach care across religious differences without presenting kindness as conditional on conversion. The funeral episode is used for recognition of human dignity, not to settle the detailed legal ruling on standing for funerals. Aishah's races are presented without body commentary, invented ages or a universal rule about every form of recreation. The boy's turn illustrates respect for his permission; ordinary queues are an application, not a complete account of drink-serving rules. Abu Dharr's correction concerns the reported insult involving another person's mother; no unsupported identification, quotation or added story is supplied. Brotherhood means the established supportive bond between an emigrant and a helper, not biological kinship or an assertion of later inheritance rules. The Quba episode does not instruct children to enter physical fights. The camel repayment does not require extra repayment, create a financial ruling or permit an agreed interest charge. The food-seller episode concerns disclosure of the wet food and does not declare a specific child's religious status. The tailor's meal is used to teach respectful companionship without creating an obligation to accept every invitation or consume unsuitable food. The Hudaybiyyah question concerns the specific advice from Umm Salamah and the Prophet's subsequent example, not an invented treaty consultation or a rule requiring children to perform adult rites. The shared donkey ride supplies no unsupported age for Usamah and is not a riding-safety instruction. The dua for Ibn Abbas concerns understanding religion, without a promise that dua replaces study. His prayer position is taught through the narrated event, not a comprehensive prayer manual or a requirement for children to stay awake at night. The Suffah account is used for inclusive hospitality without inventing a natural explanation or general promise that small quantities will always feed any group. The mat account concerns modest surroundings and does not forbid comfort, needed support or ordinary possessions. Care for Khadijah's friends is limited to the reported gifts and remembrance, without invented messages or encounters. Salman's advice is taught as balancing due rights; the school routine is an adult-guided application, not a detailed fasting ruling. This remains a draft for scholarly and child-readability review, not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: How many times did the Prophet ﷺ repeat words in Anas's report to help people understand?

options.text: Three times
Two times
Four times
Five times

questions.explanation: Anas described the Prophet ﷺ repeating words three times so listeners could understand. Helping people learn mattered.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet ﷺ have a silver ring made when preparing to send a letter?

options.text: To pay the messenger
To stamp the letter
To measure the paper
To decorate the envelope

questions.explanation: He learned that the recipients required a stamp. The ring served as a seal for his letters.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ do when a Jewish boy who served him became ill?

options.text: Sent him a work schedule
Waited for him to return
Visited the boy
Asked him to visit instead

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ went to the sick boy and sat near him. The report shows personal concern across religious differences.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ do when a Jewish funeral procession passed him?

options.text: Asked for another route
Called the procession back
Stopped it to give a speech
Stood up

questions.explanation: When told the deceased was Jewish, he pointed to the person's humanity. This episode teaches respect for human life.

questions.question: Which playful activity did Aishah describe doing with the Prophet ﷺ during journeys?

options.text: Racing on foot
Racing boats
Climbing a mountain
Playing a board game

questions.explanation: Aishah described footraces with the Prophet ﷺ. Their shared enjoyment is a warm part of his family life.

questions.question: Before offering a drink to elders on his left, what did the Prophet ﷺ ask the boy on his right?

options.text: Permission to end the gathering
Permission to let them drink first
Whether he knew their names
Whether he had washed the cup

questions.explanation: He asked the boy's permission to change the order. When the boy declined, he gave the drink to him.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ correct Abu Dharr for in this report?

options.text: Asking a question about prayer
Wearing a simple cloak
Insulting a person through his mother
Sharing food with a worker

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ challenged the insult. A person's mother or family background should not become a target for abuse.

questions.question: What bond did the Prophet ﷺ establish between Abdur Rahman ibn Awf and Sad ibn al-Rabi in Madinah?

options.text: A family relationship by birth
An agreement to travel together
A contest between traders
Brotherhood between believers

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ joined them in brotherhood. This created a relationship of support between an emigrant and a helper in Madinah.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ set out to do after hearing about fighting among people of Quba?

options.text: Help them make peace
Choose the strongest group
Watch the fight from nearby
Wait for a larger crowd

questions.explanation: He went to bring the people together in peace. Children should seek trusted adult help when conflict becomes unsafe.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ approve when only an older camel was available to repay a camel debt?

options.text: Returning nothing at all
Giving the older camel
Keeping both camels
Asking the owner to forget it

questions.explanation: He ordered that the available older camel be given. The report praises repaying what is owed in a good manner.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ find hidden beneath the dry surface of food being sold?

options.text: A different kind of coin
A measuring rope
Food wet from rain
A handwritten shopping list

questions.explanation: He said the wet food should be visible to buyers. Hiding its condition would mislead them.

questions.question: Whose invitation to a meal did the Prophet ﷺ accept in Anas's report?

options.text: A governor's
A shipbuilder's
A farmer's
A tailor's

questions.explanation: Anas accompanied the Prophet ﷺ to a tailor's meal. The host's ordinary occupation did not prevent warm companionship.

questions.question: Whose advice did the Prophet ﷺ follow when companions hesitated to complete their rites at Hudaybiyyah?

options.text: Umm Salamah's
Asma's
Fatimah's
Hafsah's

questions.explanation: Umm Salamah advised him to begin the rites himself. He acted on her advice, and the companions followed his example.

questions.question: Who rode behind the Prophet ﷺ on a donkey in this report?

options.text: Abu Hurayrah
Usamah ibn Zayd
Abdur Rahman ibn Awf
Sad ibn al-Rabi

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ let Usamah ride behind him on a donkey. This was a simple journey shared with a companion.

questions.question: After Ibn Abbas provided water for him, what did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah to give Ibn Abbas?

options.text: Leadership of a trading caravan
A larger house
Understanding of religion
A place in every competition

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for Ibn Abbas to understand religion. His response encouraged a young companion with a meaningful dua.

questions.question: When Ibn Abbas stood on his left during night prayer, where did the Prophet ﷺ move him?

options.text: Far outside the room
Behind a closed door
In front of him
To his right

questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas joined the Prophet ﷺ in prayer. The Prophet ﷺ guided him from his left side to his right.

questions.question: Which group did the Prophet ﷺ ask Abu Hurayrah to invite to share milk?

options.text: The people of Suffah
A group of visiting traders
Only the city's wealthy families
The guards of a caravan

questions.explanation: The people of Suffah needed support. The Prophet ﷺ invited them to share the milk rather than keeping it for himself.

questions.question: What was the Prophet ﷺ resting on when Umar visited him in this account?

options.text: A silk mattress
A mat of palm leaves
A cushion filled with coins
A decorated royal throne

questions.explanation: Umar saw the Prophet ﷺ resting on a simple mat. His modest surroundings did not lessen his honor.

questions.question: To whom did the Prophet ﷺ send portions of meat while remembering Khadijah?

options.text: Only visiting rulers
Only the market traders
Khadijah's women friends
The caravan guards

questions.explanation: He remembered Khadijah and sent food to her friends. His care continued through the relationships connected with her.

questions.question: Whose advice about the rights of Allah, oneself and family did the Prophet ﷺ confirm as true?

options.text: Abu Hurayrah's
Usamah's
Ibn Abbas's
Salman's

questions.explanation: Salman reminded Abu al-Darda to give each their due. The Prophet ﷺ approved this balanced advice.

questions.question: What best explains the repetition in Anas's description of the Prophet's ﷺ teaching?

options.text: Helping listeners understand the message
Making every conversation last longer
Testing how loudly people could speak
Replacing every explanation with counting

questions.explanation: Repeating an important point can support understanding. The purpose here was helping listeners, not making learning unnecessarily difficult.

questions.question: What connection explains the Prophet's ﷺ use of a ring as a letter seal?

options.text: Changing the message to please everyone
Learning a requirement and preparing accordingly
Avoiding all contact with other peoples
Sending valuable gifts instead of writing

questions.explanation: The ring met a practical requirement for receiving letters. The episode connects communication with thoughtful preparation.

questions.question: Which statement fits the Prophet's ﷺ visit to the sick Jewish boy?

options.text: He only visited relatives when they were sick
He waited until the boy could work again
He showed concern for someone of another religion
He avoided sitting near anyone who needed care

questions.explanation: The visit shows care for a sick person beyond one's own religious community. It was a personal visit, not merely an instruction.

questions.question: Which idea best explains the Prophet's ﷺ response about the Jewish funeral?

options.text: Respect is limited to one's own community
A crowd's size decides a person's value
Wealth determines how a person is treated
A person's humanity deserves recognition

questions.explanation: His response recognized the deceased person's humanity. Respectful treatment need not depend on sharing the same religion.

questions.question: What does Aishah's account of racing with the Prophet ﷺ help us understand?

options.text: His family life included playful companionship
He never took part in recreation
Family life was only about giving instructions
He expected to win every friendly activity

questions.explanation: The races show shared enjoyment within family life. Worship and responsibility do not make kind, suitable recreation meaningless.

questions.question: What makes the account of the boy's drink turn especially thoughtful?

options.text: The elders decided what the boy wanted
The boy's permission mattered despite his age
The youngest person had to remain silent
The drink was given to whoever demanded it

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ asked instead of simply overlooking the boy. The boy's place in the order was respected.

questions.question: Which distinction fits the Prophet's ﷺ correction of Abu Dharr?

options.text: Disagreement allows insults about a person's parents
A respected person never needs correction
Correcting conduct differs from insulting someone's family
Anger makes hurtful remarks acceptable

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ corrected a respected companion's hurtful conduct. Respect for someone does not make every action beyond correction.

questions.question: Which two groups did the bond between Abdur Rahman and Sad help bring together?

options.text: Two competing royal families
Only travelers from the same household
Two groups preparing to leave Madinah
Emigrants from Makkah and helpers in Madinah

questions.explanation: Abdur Rahman was an emigrant and Sad a helper in Madinah. Their brotherhood connected people through mutual care rather than shared birthplace.

questions.question: Which description fits the Prophet's ﷺ response to the conflict at Quba?

options.text: Taking action to restore peace
Treating conflict as entertainment
Choosing sides through a shouting contest
Spreading the news to embarrass everyone

questions.explanation: He responded by seeking reconciliation. Restoring peace was more useful than encouraging the conflict or gathering spectators.

questions.question: What lesson connects the camel repayment with everyday responsibility?

options.text: A borrower may decide repayment is unnecessary
Return what is owed with care
Only large debts deserve attention
An apology always replaces returning property

questions.explanation: The report praises good repayment. Its everyday lesson is responsible treatment of another person's property and rights.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet ﷺ want the wet food placed where buyers could see it?

options.text: So the seller could avoid answering questions
So every buyer would pay the highest price
So buyers could know its true condition
So appearance would matter more than truth

questions.explanation: Buyers should not be misled by a dry surface hiding wet food. Honesty includes making relevant information visible.

questions.question: Which lesson fits the Prophet's ﷺ acceptance of the tailor's meal?

options.text: Only wealthy hosts deserve a guest's attention
An impressive home is required for kindness
A person's job determines their human worth
Ordinary working people deserve respectful companionship

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ accepted a working person's hospitality. A modest meal or ordinary occupation is no reason to belittle a host.

questions.question: What did following Umm Salamah's advice demonstrate at Hudaybiyyah?

options.text: Valuing wise advice and leading by example
Accepting advice only from the loudest person
Avoiding advice whenever a problem is difficult
Waiting for everyone to act without guidance

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ listened to Umm Salamah and acted. His example helped the companions move forward.

questions.question: Which conclusion fits the Prophet's ﷺ shared donkey ride with Usamah?

options.text: Honor requires the most expensive transport
A respected leader can use simple transport
Sharing a ride always lowers someone's status
Companionship matters only on grand journeys

questions.explanation: The account shows a simple shared ride. A person's dignity does not depend on impressive transport.

questions.question: Which quality did the Prophet ﷺ especially ask Allah to develop in Ibn Abbas after his help?

options.text: Fame, rather than careful learning
Wealth, rather than useful knowledge
Understanding, rather than merely public recognition
Strength, rather than thoughtful questions

questions.explanation: The dua was for understanding religion. It highlights meaningful learning, not simply collecting praise or appearing knowledgeable.

questions.question: What does the prayer incident show about learning through practice?

options.text: Only perfect learners may join an activity
Every mistake requires a public speech
Watching from far away is the only way to learn
A learner can receive guidance while taking part

questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas joined the prayer and received guidance about his position. Learning can include correction during practice.

questions.question: What does inviting the people of Suffah show about the Prophet's ﷺ hospitality?

options.text: Remembering people who needed support
Reserving gifts for people with high status
Waiting for guests to bring expensive presents
Sharing only when there is no effort involved

questions.explanation: The invitation included people with little support. The report connects receiving a gift with remembering others' needs.

questions.question: Which lesson fits the Prophet's ﷺ simple resting place in Umar's account?

options.text: Comfortable bedding is always forbidden
Honor is not measured by luxury
Expensive possessions prove stronger faith
People must make themselves uncomfortable to be good

questions.explanation: His simple surroundings did not reduce his honor. The report does not make discomfort a requirement for children.

questions.question: What connection explains the Prophet's ﷺ gifts to Khadijah's friends?

options.text: Keeping friendships only while gifts are exchanged
Forgetting past relationships when life changes
Remembering someone through kindness to their friends
Choosing friends according to their wealth

questions.explanation: His kindness honored a lasting connection with Khadijah. Remembering loved ones can include care for people dear to them.

questions.question: Which statement matches the advice the Prophet ﷺ approved from Salman?

options.text: Extra worship means personal needs never matter
Family care has no connection with a good routine
Rest should always replace every responsibility
Worship, personal needs and family each deserve their due

questions.explanation: Salman's advice held these rights together. The Prophet ﷺ approved giving each its proper place rather than neglecting the others.

questions.question: A younger child cannot follow your explanation. Which response reflects the purpose of the Prophet's ﷺ repetition?

options.text: Repeat the key point patiently and check understanding
Say the same words faster each time
Finish quickly without checking what they understood
Assume asking again means they are not trying

questions.explanation: Patient repetition can help a learner. You can also use simpler words or seek an adult's help when needed.

questions.question: Your class must submit a project in a particular format. Which approach connects with the Prophet's ﷺ preparation for letters?

options.text: Ignore the format because the ideas are good
Check the requirement and prepare the project accordingly
Copy someone else's name onto the project
Submit an empty page with a decorative border

questions.explanation: The letter seal met a practical requirement. Checking instructions is a useful application of thoughtful preparation.

questions.question: A classmate of another religion is unwell. Which response reflects the Prophet's ﷺ care for the sick Jewish boy?

options.text: Wait until the classmate changes religion before helping
Explain that illness makes friendship impossible
Ask a parent about a suitable way to show care
Avoid every message of concern

questions.explanation: Care can reach beyond religious differences. A parent can help you choose a considerate, appropriate way to contact or support someone who is ill.

questions.question: Someone mocks a funeral because the deceased followed another religion. What response fits the lesson of the Prophet's ﷺ reaction?

options.text: Join the joke to fit in
Decide respect depends on how rich they were
Turn their grief into a competition
Encourage respectful behavior toward the grieving people

questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ response recognized a human life. We can apply that lesson by avoiding mockery and treating grieving people with respect.

questions.question: Your family plans a safe game together. Which attitude fits the Prophet's ﷺ races with Aishah?

options.text: Enjoy the activity with kindness and good humor
Treat every loss as a personal insult
Refuse because family time cannot include fun
Change the rules secretly to guarantee a win

questions.explanation: The races illustrate playful companionship. Safe, suitable recreation can be a kind way to spend time together.

questions.question: You want to move a younger child behind you in an agreed queue. What fits the Prophet's ﷺ respect for the boy's turn?

options.text: Move the child because you are older
Ask politely and respect the child's answer
Pretend the child was never in line
Tell others the child's turn does not matter

questions.explanation: The drink account shows respect for a child's place. In an ordinary agreed queue, age alone does not justify taking someone else's turn.

questions.question: During a disagreement, you insult a friend's mother. What should you do in light of the Prophet's ﷺ correction of Abu Dharr?

options.text: Explain that anger made the insult acceptable
Repeat the insult more quietly
Stop, apologize and discuss the issue without family insults
Ask others to insult their relatives too

questions.explanation: The correction identifies family insults as wrong. Taking responsibility means stopping the harm and making a sincere effort to put it right.

questions.question: A new student arrives from another town. Which action reflects the support encouraged through brotherhood in Madinah?

options.text: Expect them to manage every difficulty alone
Include them only if they bring presents
Tell them friendship depends on being born nearby
Help them find their classroom and include them

questions.explanation: The bond joined an emigrant and a local helper. Welcoming a new student is a simple present-day application of supportive companionship.

questions.question: Two classmates start throwing things during an argument. Which response applies peacemaking safely for a child?

options.text: Move to safety and get a trusted adult
Step between them and grab their arms
Gather friends to cheer for one side
Film the fight and share it

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ sought peace at Quba. A child can support peace by getting adult help rather than entering a dangerous fight.

questions.question: You borrowed a friend's book. Which action reflects the good repayment praised in the camel account?

options.text: Keep it until your friend asks several times
Return it on time and take responsibility for any damage
Return a different book without asking
Assume friendship makes the book yours

questions.explanation: Responsible borrowing respects the owner's rights. Returning a book carefully is an everyday application, not a rule that an extra gift is required.

questions.question: You exchange a toy that has a hidden broken part. What fits the Prophet's ﷺ correction of the food seller?

options.text: Hide the damage under a sticker
Mention the damage only after the exchange
Tell the other person about the damage before agreeing
Say it works perfectly because it looks clean

questions.explanation: The seller was told to make the food's condition visible. Similarly, an honest exchange requires explaining a known fault.

questions.question: At an approved family visit, a host offers a modest meal. What reflects the Prophet's ﷺ acceptance of the tailor's hospitality?

options.text: Compare the house unfavorably with a richer friend's
Tell others the meal was too ordinary
Give attention only to the wealthiest guests
Thank the host and behave respectfully

questions.explanation: The tailor's hospitality was accepted warmly. Respect for a host does not depend on expensive food or an impressive home.

questions.question: Your group is stuck, and a teammate offers a sensible suggestion. What reflects the Prophet's ﷺ response to Umm Salamah?

options.text: Consider the suggestion and help put it into practice
Reject it because you are the group leader
Wait until the same idea comes from someone louder
Accept only ideas you thought of first

questions.explanation: Listening to useful advice is compatible with leadership. The Hudaybiyyah account also shows how action can help others follow.

questions.question: A child is teased for arriving in a simple family vehicle. What lesson fits the Prophet's ﷺ ride with Usamah?

options.text: Assume the vehicle tells you the child's worth
Treat the child respectfully regardless of the vehicle
Join the teasing to impress other children
Suggest friendship requires expensive transport

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ shared a simple donkey ride. This helps challenge the idea that impressive transport determines a person's dignity.

questions.question: You want to encourage a younger child's Islamic learning. What connects with the Prophet's ﷺ dua for Ibn Abbas?

options.text: Tell them learning matters only when others applaud
Promise that one dua replaces all study
Ask Allah to give them understanding and support their learning
Compare them harshly with another child

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah for Ibn Abbas's understanding. We can encourage learning through dua, patience and practical support.

questions.question: You make a mistake while practicing prayer with a trusted teacher. What fits Ibn Abbas's learning experience?

options.text: Decide that one mistake ends all progress
Hide every question to appear perfect
Assume correction means you are unwanted
Accept clear guidance and keep learning

questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas received guidance while praying with the Prophet ﷺ. A mistake can become part of learning with a caring teacher.

questions.question: An adult helps you organize snacks for a group. What reflects the Prophet's ﷺ invitation to the people of Suffah?

options.text: Help include children who might otherwise be left out
Reserve everything for the most popular children
Require everyone to bring you a gift first
Hide the snacks until the group leaves

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ remembered people needing support. Sharing appropriately with adult guidance is a simple application of that care.

questions.question: A friend feels embarrassed about their simple bedroom. Which reassurance connects with the Prophet's ﷺ modest surroundings?

options.text: A beautiful room always means stronger faith
A person's worth is not measured by expensive furniture
Simple furniture makes someone less worthy of friendship
They must reject every comfortable item

questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ honor was not measured by luxury. We can respect simple homes without treating comfort or needed support as wrong.

questions.question: Your parent remembers an old family friend fondly. What connects with the Prophet's ﷺ kindness to Khadijah's friends?

options.text: Say old friendships never deserve attention
Contact unfamiliar people secretly without guidance
Ask your parent about sending a kind message together
Decide kindness is useful only when gifts come back

questions.explanation: He remembered Khadijah through kindness to her friends. With family guidance, we can help preserve caring relationships.

questions.question: You plan extra worship but need sleep and have family responsibilities. Which approach reflects the advice the Prophet ﷺ approved?

options.text: Skip sleep every night to prove dedication
Treat family responsibilities as always unimportant
Give up every form of worship to avoid planning
Ask an adult to help plan a balanced routine

questions.explanation: Salman's advice gave each right its due. An adult can help a child combine worship, suitable rest and family responsibilities.
